patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Resting tremor worse on the left hand

patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Hypertension, medicated with aspirin and amlodipine. Family history of schizophrenia in his mother. No other significant medical or psychiatric history.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Drinks 1-2 beers nightly and is a former cigar smoker.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies any other systemic complaints. Specifically, no urinary symptoms, no significant changes in bowel habits, no reported falls or dizziness.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with hand tremors and recent memory issues.

turns.content: Doctor: Hello—I'm Dr. Agent. To understand your hand tremor and recent memory issues, when did the tremor start and is it worse at rest or when you use your hands? Doctor: Also, have you noticed any new stiffness, slowed movements, changes in sleep (acting out dreams), or reduced sense of smell?

Patient: The tremor in my left hand started about a year ago, and it seems worse when I’m resting rather than when I’m using it. Lately I’ve also felt some stiffness and that my movements are a bit slower, and my wife says my memory has been slipping with simple tasks like paying bills.

Doctor: Thank you. Do you also notice a shuffling gait or falls, trouble swallowing/soft voice, or constipation, and have you ever started any medications that can cause tremor (e.g., antipsychotics, metoclopramide, valproate, lithium)? Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Neurology evaluation with basic labs (CBC, CMP, TSH, B12), and consider DAT-SPECT or brain MRI if needed.

RESULTS: Blood Pressure 140/85 mmHg; Heart Rate 72 bpm; Respiratory Rate 16 breaths/min; Temperature 36.7°C (98.06°F); Facial expression reduced; Speech soft and monotonous; Left hand resting tremor present (worsened by emotional stress/concentration); Mild rigidity on bilateral upper extremity manipulation. CBC: WBC 7,500/µL; Hemoglobin 14 g/dL; Platelets 230,000/µL. Thyroid: TSH 2.5 mIU/L; Free T4 1.2 ng/dL. Brain MRI: no acute abnormalities; mild age-appropriate cerebral atrophy.

Doctor: Given your resting “pill-rolling” left-hand tremor, soft/monotonous speech, reduced facial expression, mild rigidity, and mild memory/functional decline with MRI showing no acute cause, my leading concern is Parkinson’s disease rather than an essential tremor. Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Dopamine transporter (DAT-SPECT) scan (or repeat/confirm with a skilled movement-disorders neurology exam and consider a levodopa response trial). Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Medication review and screen for red flags; also consider cognitive testing (MoCA) to better characterize the memory issues. DIAGNOSIS READY: Parkinson’s disease (likely with mild cognitive impairment)
